# AutoComplete A text input with a suggestions list. Works in two modes: **static** (filters a provided `items` array as the user types) or **async** (resolves suggestions via `onSearch`, debounced, with a loading state). ## Mental model The input manages its own text internally; you react to a chosen suggestion via `onItemClick(value)`. components.name: Chat
components.description: A messaging surface: a scrollable transcript of message bubbles plus a composer.
components.content:
# Chat A messaging surface: a scrollable transcript of message bubbles plus a composer. ## Mental model Chat is **controlled**: you own the `messages` array; the composer reports text via `onSend` (you append and re-render). Each message carries an `authorId`; those matching `currentUserId` align right in the accent colour, everyone else aligns left on a raised surface with an avatar (image or initials of `authorName`) and name. Consecutive messages from one author **group** (one avatar + name per group, timestamp on the last bubble). The list **auto-scrolls** to the newest message unless you've scrolled up to read history, in which case a "jump to latest" button appears. `typingNames` shows an animated indicator. ## Quick start ```tsx const [messages, setMessages] = useState(initial) { setMessages((m) => [...m, { id: uid(), authorId: 'me', text, timestamp: new Date(), status: 'sent' }]) }} /> ``` Enter sends; Shift+Enter inserts a newline. Use `hideComposer` for a read-only transcript. ## Loading history Chat doesn't fetch: you do: but it gives you a transcript **skeleton** for the first load via `loading`. Show it while a history request is in flight, then hand over the messages: ```tsx const [messages, setMessages] = useState([]) const [loading, setLoading] = useState(true) useEffect(() => { fetch('/api/chat/history') .then((r) => r.json()) .then(setMessages) .finally(() => setLoading(false)) }, []) ``` See the **Async history: MSW (HTTP)** story (mocked with Mock Service Worker). ## Real-time with a WebSocket Because Chat is controlled, wiring it to a socket is just "push inbound frames into state, send outbound on the composer." Drive the header `subtitle` and `loading` from the connection state for a complete feel: ```tsx const [messages, setMessages] = useState([]) const [status, setStatus] = useState<'connecting' | 'online' | 'offline'>('connecting') const socket = useRef(null) useEffect(() => { const ws = new WebSocket('wss://…/room/42') socket.current = ws ws.onopen = () => setStatus('online') ws.onclose = () => setStatus('offline') ws.onmessage = (e) => setMessages((m) => [...m, JSON.parse(e.data)]) return () => ws.close() }, []) const send = (text: string) => { setMessages((m) => [...m, { id: uid(), authorId: 'me', text, timestamp: new Date(), status: 'sent' }]) // optimistic socket.current?.send(JSON.stringify({ text })) } ``` The same shape works for socket.io / SSE / any push transport. See the **Real-time: WebSocket (MSW ws)** story (a live `WebSocket` mocked end-to-end by MSW). ## API reference

# Icons A cohesive pack of SVG icons that colour with `currentColor`, size in pixels, and are accessible by default. Browse them all in **Icons → Gallery** (click any icon to copy its usage). ## Mental model Every icon is a small React component drawn on a 24×24 grid. It has **no hard-coded colour or size**: it inherits the surrounding text colour via `currentColor` and defaults to 24px. Most icons are outline (stroked); a few are solid (carets, dots, `StarFilled`). Icons are **decorative by default** (`aria-hidden`); pass a `title` only when the icon is the sole meaning of a control. There are **two ways to import**, by design: ```tsx // 1) Tree-shakeable named imports from the /icons subpath: ship only what you // use. Best for app code. Every icon is available here (no name clashes). // 2) The Icon.* namespace from the root entry: quick and discoverable. Lives // on the root so it never clashes with component names (there's both a // `Table` component and a `Table` icon). ``` ```tsx // 24px, inherits text colour // follows the button colour ``` Per-icon tree-shaking is real: importing a single icon from `@geomak/ui/icons` bundles ~0.7 KB, not the whole set (each definition is `/* @__PURE__ */`-annotated and the package is marked side-effect-free). ## Colour & size Because icons use `currentColor`, set colour with a text utility on the icon or any ancestor: ```tsx ``` Size is a pixel number (or any CSS length). Outline icons accept `strokeWidth` (default `1.5`): ```tsx ``` The `Spinner` icon is static markup: add `className="animate-spin"` to rotate it. ## Accessibility

Draw the artwork on a 24×24 grid (or set a custom `viewBox`). ```tsx // Outline (default): paths use stroke="currentColor", round caps/joins. const Anchor = createIcon('Anchor', ) // Solid: fill="currentColor". const Pin = createIcon('Pin', , { solid: true }) ```

Each panel positions itself under the bar and its sections spread across a content-sized grid. Below the `md` breakpoint the whole bar collapses into a tap-friendly hamburger accordion. ## Mental model `MegaMenu` is **compositional**. The bar holds top-level items; each item is either a **panel item** (opens a dropdown) or a **plain link**. - `MegaMenu.Item label`: a top-level entry. With children → opens a panel. With only `href` → a plain top-level link. - `MegaMenu.Panel`: the dropdown layout (a grid of sections + an optional featured column). - `MegaMenu.Section title`: a titled column of links. - `MegaMenu.Link`: a rich link: icon (in a tinted square) + title + description. - `MegaMenu.Featured`: a highlighted promo column (raised surface). The library is **router-agnostic**: links take `href` and/or `onClick`. Wire them to your router (e.g. wrap with your `` or call `navigate` in `onClick`). ## Quick start ```tsx } description="Dashboards & reports"> Analytics } description="Real-time events"> Streams } description="Policies & audit" active> Security } /> ``` ## A featured (promo) column `MegaMenu.Featured` sits beside the sections as a raised callout. Predictive maintenance in one console.

Explore → ``` ## Panel width Each panel lays its sections out on a grid with a *definite* width, so sections spread to fill rather than shrink-wrapping to their text. # Scheduler An event scheduler with **month** and **week** views: the agenda-style calendar for dashboards and ops tools. For single-date selection use the [DatePicker](/docs/inputs-datepicker--docs) input instead. ## Mental model The Scheduler owns the view (`month` / `week`) and the focused date; the toolbar pages and toggles them. Click the month/year title to open a quick jump picker (month grid + year stepper) for moving across the calendar fast, rather than paging one step at a time. Feed it data one of two ways: - **Controlled**: pass `events` directly (you fetch / manage them). - **Async**: pass `loadEvents(range, view)`; it's called whenever the visible range or view changes, and the Scheduler shows a loading indicator around it. Events span a `start`–`end` (ISO strings or `Date`s). In **month** view they render as coloured chips per day (capped, with "+N more"); in **week** view they sit at their real time, sized by duration, inside a scrollable hour grid. ## Quick start ```tsx // Async: fetch per visible range api.events(from, to)} onSelectEvent={(e) => openEvent(e)} onNewEvent={() => createEvent()} /> // Controlled createAt(d)} /> ``` ## Creating, editing & deleting events The Scheduler is **read-oriented**: it renders events and reports intent, but it owns no event form or persistence (your API, validation, and modals stay yours). Wire the callbacks to your own flow, then update `events` (or let `loadEvents` refetch): - **Create**: `onSelectSlot(date)` fires when an empty day cell (month) or time slot (week) is clicked; `onNewEvent()` fires from the toolbar button. - **Edit / delete**: `onSelectEvent(event)` fires when an event is clicked; open your editor (e.g. a `Modal`) and mutate from there. ```tsx const [events, setEvents] = useState(initial) openCreateModal(date)} onSelectEvent={(e) => openEditModal(e)} // edit or delete inside the modal /> ``` See the **Create / delete (controlled)** story for a working example. ## Loading & errors With `loadEvents`, the Scheduler manages the async states for you: - **First load** shows a grid-shaped **skeleton**; background refetches (paging with events already on screen) show a subtle spinner by the title instead. - **Failure** is surfaced, not swallowed: a **retry** state replaces the grid and the optional `onError(error)` callback fires. (Earlier behaviour silently showed an empty calendar; it no longer does.) See the **Async error + retry** story. ## API reference

components.name: SecureLayout
components.description: A layout wrapper that gates its children behind an access check none
components.content:
# SecureLayout A layout wrapper that gates its children behind an access check none authentication, RBAC (roles), PBAC (permissions), JWT expiry, and/or a custom (optionally async) predicate. > **This is a UI guard, not a security boundary.** It controls what renders. > Real authorization must be enforced by your API/server: never trust a > client-side check. The JWT is only inspected for expiry; its signature is > **not** verified here. ## Mental model The check runs in an effect (so async predicates are supported). While it resolves, the `loadingFallback` shows; on success the children fade in; on failure the `fallback` renders and `onDeny` fires (e.g. to redirect). The gates are evaluated in order and **all** must pass: 1. **Authenticated**: `isAuthenticated`, or inferred from `token` validity, or assumed true if neither is given. 2. **Roles (RBAC)**: `requiredRoles` against `roles` (any, or all with `requireAllRoles`). 3. **Permissions (PBAC)**: `requiredPermissions` against `permissions` (any, or all with `requireAllPermissions`). 4. **`canAccess()`**: the final say; may be async. Every prop except `children` is optional: use as much or as little as you need. The two ends of the spectrum: ## Simple: JWT-only bootstrap (no roles/permissions) The common case: on load, validate the JWT, hydrate app state from the server, then land the user. Everything custom goes in `canAccess`; `onGranted` / `onDeny` handle the navigation. Synchronous gates resolve on the first render (no spinner flash); `fallback={null}` avoids a panel flashing while you redirect. ```tsx { const jwt = localStorage.getItem('jwt') if (!jwt) return false await tokenLogin(jwt) // validate + hydrate app state return true }} onGranted={() => navigate('/dashboard')} onDeny={() => navigate('/logout')} fallback={null} > ``` Even simpler: gate purely on a token's validity: ```tsx navigate('/login')}> ``` ## Per-route: one wrapper, decision per path To gate *different routes* from a **single** wrapper around the whole app, pass the current path as `route` (from your router). The check re-runs whenever `route` changes (i.e. on navigation), and `canAccess` receives the path so it can decide per route. Keep `canAccess` **synchronous** (consult an in-memory route → roles map) and there's no loading flash on navigation. ```tsx const allowed = { '/admin': ['admin'], '/reports': ['analyst', 'admin'] } (allowed[path] ?? []).some((r) => user.roles.includes(r))} onDeny={() => navigate('/403')} > ``` Without `route`, the check runs on mount and refresh only: so a root wrapper gates the *app* (and re-bootstraps on reload) but does **not** re-evaluate on client-side navigation. Add `route` to make one wrapper guard every path; or nest a SecureLayout inside individual routes if they need independent gates. ## Full: RBAC + PBAC gate ```tsx navigate('/login')} > ``` ## API reference
PropTypeDefaultDescription
childrenReactNodenoneProtected content.
isAuthenticatedbooleannoneAuth flag; inferred from token if omitted, else assumed true.
tokenstringnoneJWT: checked for expiry (exp) only.
roles / requiredRolesstring[]noneUser roles vs. required (RBAC).
requireAllRolesbooleanfalseRequire all roles, not just one.
permissions / requiredPermissionsstring[]noneUser perms vs. required (PBAC).
requireAllPermissionsbooleanfalseRequire all permissions.
routestringnoneCurrent path (e.g. location.pathname). Makes the check re-run on navigation and is passed to canAccess: enables per-route gating from one wrapper.
canAccess{'(route?) => boolean | Promise'}noneFinal predicate (may be async); receives the route. The hook for custom / token-login / per-route logic.
loadingFallbackReactNodespinnerShown while checking. null → render nothing.
fallbackReactNode"Access denied" panelShown when denied. null → render nothing (redirect flows).
onGranted{'() => void'}noneFired once on grant (e.g. hydrate state, redirect to a landing route).
onDeny{'() => void'}noneFired once on denial (e.g. redirect to login/logout).
See the **Layout → SecureLayout** stories.

# Tabs Switch between sibling content panes. The active tab is marked by a thin cobalt indicator that **slides** between tabs like a needle settling on a gauge, never a heavy full-fill pill. Built on Radix Tabs, so roving-tabindex keyboard nav, `role="tablist"`/`tab`/`tabpanel`, and reduced-motion all come for free. ## Mental model `Tabs` is **compositional**: the root holds the active value + shared options (variant, size, orientation), and you assemble the parts yourself: - `Tabs.List`: the strip. Owns overflow (scroll + fade + chevrons + a "jump to any tab" menu) and the sliding marker context. - `Tabs.Trigger value`: one tab button. Self-registers so the overflow menu can list it. - `Tabs.Panel value`: the matching content pane. Lazy by default; mounts on first activation. - `Tabs.Add`: an optional trailing "+" affordance for dynamic tabs. A `Trigger` and its `Panel` are paired by `value`. Provide `defaultValue` (uncontrolled) or `value` + `onChange` (controlled). ## Quick start ```tsx Overview Activity Settings … … … ``` ## Variants Set `variant` on the root. The marker animates (exponential ease-out, reduced motion → instant) in `underline` and `segmented`. ```tsx // Underline (default, signature): sliding cobalt marker under the active tab. … // Segmented: a lifted-pill track for 2–4 compact options; the pill slides. Day Week Month … // Enclosed: folder tabs. The active tab is a raised surface that joins the // panel: wrap the panels in a bordered, top-flush container. Editor Preview
… …
``` ## Orientation & size ```tsx // Vertical rail + panel beside it. Triggers left-align and fill the rail. Profile Alerts … … // Sizes: sm | md (default) | lg. … ``` ## Icons & count badges ```tsx }>Overview Activity Archived ``` The badge is a subtle, theme-relative chip (slate pill + near-white text) that self-inverts in dark mode. ## Dynamic tabs (closeable + add) Compose the tab list from your own state; `Tabs.Trigger closeable` renders an ×, and `Tabs.Add` a trailing "+". ```tsx function Workspace() { const [tabs, setTabs] = useState([{ key: 't1', title: 'Aurora' }]) const [active, setActive] = useState('t1') const [seq, setSeq] = useState(2) const close = (key) => setTabs((p) => { const next = p.filter((t) => t.key !== key) if (key === active && next.length) setActive(next[next.length - 1].key) return next }) const add = () => { const key = `t${seq}` setTabs((p) => [...p, { key, title: `Vessel ${seq}` }]) setActive(key); setSeq((s) => s + 1) } return ( {tabs.map((t) => ( close(t.key)}> {t.title} ))} {tabs.map((t) => …)} ) } ``` ## Overflow When the strip is too narrow for its tabs it scrolls (drag / wheel / swipe), the edges fade, and prev/next chevrons appear **only on the overflowing side**. A **"Show all tabs" (⋯) menu** also appears: hover or click it to jump straight to any tab. The picked (or keyboard-activated) tab scrolls into view automatically. No configuration needed. ## Lazy vs. kept-mounted panels ```tsx // Default: panels mount on first activation (lazy). … // keepMounted: render even when inactive (preserves scroll / form state). … ``` ## Keyboard & accessibility
KeyAction
← / →Move between tabs (horizontal). Activates on focus.
↑ / ↓Move between tabs (vertical).
Home / EndFirst / last tab.
TabMove focus out of the list into the active panel.
EscClose the overflow "all tabs" menu.
Roles (`tablist` / `tab` / `tabpanel`) and focus management come from Radix. Give `Tabs.List` an `aria-label`. The close button and add button have accessible names. The marker honours `prefers-reduced-motion`. ## API reference ### ``
PropTypeDefaultDescription

defaultValuestringnoneUncontrolled initial active tab.
onChange{'(value) => void'}noneFires with the next active value.
variant'underline' | 'segmented' | 'enclosed''underline'Visual style.
size'sm' | 'md' | 'lg''md'Control height + type scale.
orientation'horizontal' | 'vertical''horizontal'Strip-above vs. rail-beside.
className / stylestring / CSSPropertiesnoneMerged onto the root.
### ``
PropTypeDescription
valuestringRequired. Pairs with a `Tabs.Panel`.
iconReactNodeLeading icon.
badgeReactNodeTrailing count chip.
closeable / onCloseboolean / {'() => void'}Render a × and handle close.

### ``

### `` / `` `Tabs.List` takes `aria-label` (recommended) + `className`. `Tabs.Add` takes `onClick`, `aria-label` (default "Add tab"), and `className`. ```ts ``` See the **Data Display → Tabs** stories for every variant and state, live.

# ThemeSwitch A dark-mode toggle built on Radix Switch. # useBreakpoint A reactive view of the library's responsive breakpoints: for layout decisions that live in JavaScript (which component to render, how many columns, etc.). ## Mental model `useBreakpoint()` is built on [useMediaQuery](/docs/hooks-usemediaquery-guide--docs) and exposes the same breakpoints as the Tailwind `screens` config. Each flag is a **min-width** match (mobile-first): `md` is `true` at ≥ 768px. `active` is the largest breakpoint currently met, or `'base'` below `sm`. It's SSR-safe: every flag is `false` until mounted, then syncs. ## Breakpoints
FlagMin widthTrue when
sm480pxviewport ≥ 480
md768pxviewport ≥ 768
lg976pxviewport ≥ 976
xl1440pxviewport ≥ 1440
activenoneThe largest matched flag, or 'base' below sm.
## Quick start ```tsx function Nav() { const { md, active } = useBreakpoint() if (!md) return // below 768px return } ``` For an arbitrary one-off query (orientation, reduced-motion, print, a custom width) reach for `useMediaQuery(query)` directly. See the **Hooks → useBreakpoint** story (resize the viewport to watch it update).

components.name: useJwt
components.description: Decode a JWT client-side and track its expiry reactively.
components.content:
# useJwt Decode a JWT client-side and track its expiry reactively. > **Decode only: never verification.** The hook reads the token's claims; it > does not (and cannot) verify the signature. Treat the result as a UI hint; > real authorization belongs on the server. Pairs naturally with > [SecureLayout](/docs/layout-securelayout-guide--docs). ## Mental model `useJwt(token)` decodes the header and payload and derives expiry from the `exp` claim. It re-renders **exactly when the token crosses its `exp`**, so `isExpired` / `isValid` flip on their own without polling. components.content:
# useDownload

A stateless hook that owns the single implementation of the **blob to object-URL to anchor to click to deferred revoke** pattern. Both `useExcel` and `usePdf` delegate their browser-download step here.

```tsx

const { saveBlob, saveFromBase64 } = useDownload()
```

---

## Return type

```ts
interface UseDownloadReturn {
  saveBlob(blob: Blob, fileName: string): void
  saveFromBase64(base64: string, fileName: string, mimeType?: string): void
}
```

Both functions have stable identities (`useCallback` with stable deps). They are safe to pass as event-handler props without causing re-renders.

---

## saveBlob

```ts
saveBlob(blob: Blob, fileName: string): void
```

Triggers a browser download for any `Blob`.

**Steps:**

1. `URL.createObjectURL(blob)` allocates a one-time URL.
2. A transient `<a download="fileName">` anchor is created (never appended to the DOM).
3. `.click()` initiates the download.
4. `setTimeout(() => URL.revokeObjectURL(url), 0)` revokes after one event-loop tick so the click registers before the URL is released.

**SSR safety:** the function checks `typeof window === 'undefined'` and returns early on the server.

```tsx
const { saveBlob } = useDownload()

const downloadCsv = () => {
  const csv = 'vessel,imo\nMV Aurora,9876543\n'
  saveBlob(new Blob([csv], { type: 'text/csv;charset=utf-8' }), 'fleet.csv')
}
```

---

## saveFromBase64

```ts
saveFromBase64(base64: string, fileName: string, mimeType?: string): void
```

Decodes a base64 string and downloads the result. Handles two input shapes:

| Input shape | MIME resolution |
|---|---|
| `data:<mime>;base64,<payload>` (data URI) | Extracted from the prefix automatically |
| `<payload>` (raw base64, no prefix) | Supplied via the `mimeType` argument |

Falls back to `'application/octet-stream'` when both the prefix and the argument are absent.

```tsx
const { saveFromBase64 } = useDownload()

// Data URI: MIME inferred from the prefix
saveFromBase64(dataUri, 'image.png')

// Raw base64: MIME supplied explicitly
saveFromBase64(rawBase64, 'report.pdf', 'application/pdf')
```

**Steps:** strip data-URI prefix, `atob(payload)`, copy into `Uint8Array`, construct `Blob`, delegate to `saveBlob`.

---

## Integration with useExcel and usePdf

You do not need `useDownload` directly if you are using the higher-level hooks. Both `useExcel.exportSheets` and `usePdf.exportCanvases` call `saveBlob` internally when no `onSave` callback is passed.

Use `useDownload` directly when you have a raw `Blob` from a `fetch` response, a WebSocket frame, or any other source outside of Excel or PDF generation.

---

## Live examples

See the stories under **Hooks > useDownload**.

components.content:
# useExcel

A hook that wraps [SheetJS (xlsx)](https://sheetjs.com/) to provide ergonomic Excel export and parse operations. The library already bundles xlsx; `useExcel` adds type safety, worksheet name sanitization, and browser-download wiring.

**xlsx is lazy-loaded.** The import happens on the first call to `exportSheets` or `readWorkbook` and is not included in the initial bundle.

```tsx

const { exportSheets, readWorkbook, isExporting } = useExcel()
```

---

## Return type

```ts
interface UseExcelReturn {
  exportSheets(sheets: ExcelSheetInput[], options?: ExportSaveOptions): Promise<void>
  readWorkbook(source: File | Blob | ArrayBuffer | Uint8Array): Promise<ParsedSheet[]>
  isExporting: boolean
}
```

---

## Types

### ExcelSheetInput

```ts
interface ExcelSheetInput {
  name: string
  columns?: string[]
  rows: Record<string, CellValue>[] | CellValue[][]
}

type CellValue = string | number | boolean | null | undefined | Date
```

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `name` | Worksheet name. Sanitized automatically (max 31 chars, restricted chars replaced with `_`). |
| `columns` | Optional explicit column order used as the bold header row. Inferred from row-object keys when omitted. |
| `rows` | Array of key-value objects or positional `CellValue` arrays. Both shapes are supported and can be mixed across sheets. |

### ExportSaveOptions

```ts
interface ExportSaveOptions {
  fileName?: string
  onSave?: (blob: Blob, name: string) => void | Promise<void>
}
```

| Field | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `fileName` | `'export'` | File name without extension. `.xlsx` is appended automatically. |
| `onSave` | none | When provided, receives the Blob instead of triggering a download. |

### ParsedSheet

```ts
interface ParsedSheet {
  name: string
  rows: Record<string, CellValue>[]
}
```

---

## exportSheets

Builds a `.xlsx` workbook and either triggers a browser download or calls `onSave`.

Per worksheet:

1. Header row is written bold, from `columns` or derived from the union of all row-object keys.
2. Object rows are mapped by key order; array rows are written positionally.
3. Column widths are auto-sized from the longest cell value, capped at 40 characters.
4. Worksheet names longer than 31 characters are truncated; the characters `\ / ? * [ ] :` are replaced with `_`.

```tsx
const { exportSheets, isExporting } = useExcel()

// Object rows with explicit column order
await exportSheets(
  [
    {
      name: 'Fleet',
      columns: ['Vessel', 'IMO', 'DWT (t)', 'CII'],
      rows: [
        { Vessel: 'MV Aurora', IMO: 9876543, 'DWT (t)': 81200, CII: 'B' },
        { Vessel: 'MV Borealis', IMO: 9123456, 'DWT (t)': 115000, CII: 'C' },
      ],
    },
  ],
  { fileName: 'fleet' }
)

// Positional array rows
await exportSheets(
  [
    {
      name: 'Cargo',
      columns: ['Port', 'Cargo (t)', 'ETD'],
      rows: [
        ['Rotterdam', 42000, '2024-03-12'],
        ['Singapore', 38500, '2024-03-28'],
      ],
    },
  ],
  { fileName: 'cargo' }
)
```

### Upload instead of download

```tsx
await exportSheets([sheet], {
  onSave: async (blob, name) => {
    await fetch('/api/upload', { method: 'POST', body: blob })
  },
})
```

---

## readWorkbook

Parses any Excel workbook. Returns one `ParsedSheet` per worksheet. The first row of each worksheet becomes the header keys; all subsequent rows become `Record<header, CellValue>`.

```tsx
const { readWorkbook } = useExcel()

// From a file picker
const [parsed] = await readWorkbook(event.target.files[0])
console.log(parsed.name)  // worksheet name
console.log(parsed.rows)  // [{ Vessel: 'MV Aurora', ... }]

// From a fetch response
const buf = await fetch('/api/data.xlsx').then(r => r.arrayBuffer())
const sheets = await readWorkbook(buf)
```

Empty worksheets return `rows: []`. They are not skipped.

---

## isExporting

`isExporting` is `true` while `exportSheets` is running. Use it to disable buttons and show loading indicators:

```tsx
<Button disabled={isExporting} onClick={() => exportSheets([sheet])}>
  {isExporting ? 'Building...' : 'Download .xlsx'}
</Button>
```

`readWorkbook` does not set `isExporting`.

---

## Live examples

See the stories under **Hooks > useExcel**.

components.content:
# usePdf

A hook that wraps [jsPDF](https://github.com/parallax/jsPDF) to export one or more `HTMLCanvasElement` objects as a multi-page PDF. The library already bundles jsPDF; `usePdf` adds orientation handling, aspect-ratio-preserving scaling, title headers, and browser-download wiring.

**jsPDF is lazy-loaded.** The import happens on the first `exportCanvases` call and is not included in the initial bundle.

```tsx

const { exportCanvases, isExporting } = usePdf()
```

---

## Return type

```ts
interface UsePdfReturn {
  exportCanvases(pages: PdfPage[], options?: PdfExportOptions): Promise<void>
  isExporting: boolean
}
```

---

## Types

### PdfPage

```ts
interface PdfPage {
  canvas: HTMLCanvasElement
  title?: string
}
```

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `canvas` | The source canvas. Canvases with `width === 0` or `height === 0` are silently skipped. |
| `title` | Optional page heading. Rendered bold and centered, reserving 28 px at the top of the page. |

### PdfExportOptions

```ts
interface PdfExportOptions {
  fileName?: string
  orientation?: 'landscape' | 'portrait'
  onSave?: (blob: Blob, name: string) => void | Promise<void>
}
```

| Field | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `fileName` | `'export'` | File name without extension. `.pdf` is appended automatically. |
| `orientation` | `'landscape'` | Page orientation. |
| `onSave` | none | When provided, receives the Blob instead of triggering a download. |

---

## exportCanvases

Converts an array of canvases into a PDF document and either triggers a browser download or calls `onSave`.

**Per page:**

1. `canvas.toDataURL('image/png')` captures the current pixel content.
2. If `title` is set, 28 px is reserved at the top for a bold centered heading.
3. The canvas image is scaled to fill the remaining page area, preserving the canvas aspect ratio (letterboxed, never stretched or cropped).
4. The image is added to the jsPDF document.

Canvases with zero dimensions are skipped without error.

```tsx
const { exportCanvases, isExporting } = usePdf()

// Off-screen canvas (no DOM attachment needed)
const canvas = document.createElement('canvas')
canvas.width = 800
canvas.height = 500
// ... draw your chart ...

await exportCanvases(
  [{ canvas, title: 'Fleet CO2 Emissions 2024' }],
  { fileName: 'emissions', orientation: 'landscape' }
)
```

### Multiple pages

```tsx
await exportCanvases(
  [
    { canvas: emissionsCanvas, title: 'CO2 Emissions' },
    { canvas: fuelCanvas,      title: 'Fuel Consumption' },
    { canvas: distanceCanvas,  title: 'Distance Sailed' },
  ],
  { fileName: 'fleet-report' }
)
```

### Canvas from a charting library

```tsx
const canvasRef = useRef<HTMLCanvasElement>(null)

// After the chart has rendered:
await exportCanvases([{ canvas: canvasRef.current!, title: 'Revenue' }])
```

`canvas.toDataURL()` is called at export time, so it captures whatever the canvas holds at that moment.

### Upload instead of download

```tsx
await exportCanvases([{ canvas }], {
  onSave: async (blob, name) => {
    const form = new FormData()
    form.append('file', blob, name)
    await fetch('/api/reports', { method: 'POST', body: form })
  },
})
```

---

## isExporting

```tsx
<Button disabled={isExporting} onClick={() => exportCanvases(pages)}>
  {isExporting ? 'Generating...' : 'Export PDF'}
</Button>
```

---

## Caveats

- **Draw before export.** `canvas.toDataURL()` returns a blank image if no pixels have been painted. Ensure the chart has finished rendering before calling `exportCanvases`.
- **CORS for external images.** If the canvas draws images from cross-origin URLs, the canvas becomes tainted and `toDataURL()` throws. Use a CORS-enabled image server or proxy.
- **Image-based output.** The PDF is purely raster. Text inside a canvas is not selectable. For text-searchable PDFs, use `PdfViewer` with a server-generated PDF that includes a text layer.

---

## Live examples

See the stories under **Hooks > usePdf**.

It renders only the pages currently inside the viewport, supports a selectable text layer with in-document search, and provides a configurable toolbar with zoom, page-jump, fit controls, download, and print. **pdfjs-dist is loaded lazily.** It is not part of the entry bundle and only fetches on first render. ```tsx ``` --- ## Source types `PdfViewer` accepts four source shapes via the `source` prop.

```tsx // Show only navigation // No toolbar ``` --- ## Text layer and search When `textLayer` is `true`, invisible `` elements are overlaid on each page, aligned to PDF glyphs via transform matrices from pdfjs-dist. Text is selectable and copy-pasteable. The search bar requires `textLayer`. Search is debounced (220 ms) and highlights all matches on every rendered page simultaneously. --- ## Virtualization Only pages whose bounding box overlaps the visible viewport are rendered to canvas. Off-screen pages are represented by empty placeholder `
` elements that match the page's pixel height, keeping the scrollbar accurate. The `overscan` prop (default `2`) controls how many extra pages are rendered above and below the viewport. Increase it to reduce blank flash on fast scrolls; decrease it to reduce memory use. --- ## Worker configuration pdfjs-dist uses a Web Worker for off-thread decoding. By default the viewer injects a version-pinned CDN URL. For air-gapped environments or strict CSPs, bundle the worker and point to it: ```tsx ``` --- ## Recipes ### File from a picker ```tsx const [file, setFile] = useState(null) setFile(e.target.files?.[0] ?? null)} /> {file && } ``` ### Authenticated API fetch ```tsx const [bytes, setBytes] = useState(null) useEffect(() => { fetch('/api/report.pdf', { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${token}` } }) .then(r => r.arrayBuffer()) .then(buf => setBytes(new Uint8Array(buf))) }, []) {bytes && } ``` ### Embed without chrome ```tsx ``` ### Start on a specific page at a specific zoom ```tsx ``` --- ## Caveats - **SSR:** pdfjs-dist is imported inside a `useEffect`, so server-side rendering is safe. Supply a bundled worker via `workerSrc` to avoid this. - **Large PDFs:** For documents with hundreds of pages, set `textLayer={false}` until the user requests search. components.content:
# Spreadsheet A virtualized, multi-sheet spreadsheet component. Accepts in-memory data or user-opened files, supports inline editing with type coercion, sortable columns, context menus, and Export/Open via a File menu. xlsx and PDF export are lazy-loaded, so the initial bundle impact is near-zero. ```tsx ``` --- ## Data model ### SheetData Each `SheetData` object maps to a worksheet tab. ```ts interface SheetData { name: string columns: GridColumn[] rows: Record[] } type CellValue = string | number | boolean | null | undefined | Date ``` ### GridColumn ```ts interface GridColumn { key: string label: string width?: number align?: 'left' | 'center' | 'right' editable?: boolean type?: 'text' | 'number' | 'date' | 'boolean' } ```
FieldDefaultDescription
keyrequiredThe row-object key this column reads from.
labelrequiredDisplay text in the header row.
width120Column width in pixels. User-resizable.
align'left'Cell text alignment.
editableinherits Spreadsheet.editablePer-column editability override.
type'text'Controls input type during editing and sort comparison.
--- ## Props
PropTypeDefaultDescription
sourceSheetData[]noneIn-memory worksheet data.
editablebooleanfalseEnable inline cell editing.
sortablebooleanfalseEnable column sorting.
virtualizebooleantrueVirtualize rendering for large datasets (auto-enabled above 500 rows).
heightnumber | string'100%'Container height.
widthnumber | string'100%'Container width.
emptyRowsnumber0Append blank rows for spreadsheet-like feel. Display-only.
emptyColsnumber0Append blank columns. Display-only.
rowHeightnumber32Row height in pixels. Uniform; required for virtual scroll.
export{'\'xlsx\' | \'csv\' | \'pdf\''} | falseallControls which export formats appear in the File menu, or hides it entirely.
onCellEdit{'(edit: CellEdit) => void'}noneCalled on every cell change.
onChange{'(data: SheetData[]) => void'}noneCalled with the full updated data after any edit.
--- ## Editing Enable editing with `editable`. Each cell change fires `onCellEdit`: ```ts interface CellEdit { sheetIndex: number rowIndex: number columnKey: string value: CellValue previousValue: CellValue } ``` Controlled pattern: ```tsx const [data, setData] = useState(initialData) console.log(edit)} onChange={(next) => setData(next)} /> ``` ### Value coercion When a column has a `type` set, the raw input string is coerced before the edit event fires:
Column typeCoercion
'number'parseFloat; invalid strings become null
'boolean''true', '1', 'yes' become true; everything else becomes false
'date'new Date(value); invalid strings become null
'text'No coercion
--- ## Sorting `sortable` enables column sorting. Click a header to toggle ascending/descending/off. Sort does not mutate the `source` prop; the original order is restored when sorting is cleared. Numeric columns sort numerically, date columns sort chronologically, and all other types sort lexicographically. --- ## Sheet management When `editable` is true and `allowAddSheet` is not explicitly disabled, a **+** button appears next to the sheet tabs. Click the **x** on a tab to delete it (the last sheet cannot be deleted). Right-click a tab for rename and delete options. --- ## File menu The toolbar File menu provides:
ActionFormatsNotes
Open.xlsx, .csvParses the file with xlsx and replaces current data
Export.xlsx, .csv, .pdfBuilds the file lazily from current in-memory data
All exports use the same lazy-loaded xlsx and jsPDF modules that `useExcel` and `usePdf` use. The first export fetches the chunk; subsequent exports are instant. PDF export renders each sheet to an off-screen canvas: one page per sheet. --- ## Virtualization When `virtualize` is `true`, only rows inside the visible viewport are rendered. Row heights are uniform (`rowHeight` prop, default `32`), so the virtual scroller can compute offsets without measuring. Auto-enabled above 500 rows. Set `virtualize={false}` to render all rows (useful for printing or accessibility tools). --- ## Recipes ### Read-only display with export ```tsx ``` ### Editable controlled ```tsx const [data, setData] = useState(initialSheets) setData(next)} /> ``` ### File picker ```tsx const [file, setFile] = useState(null) setFile(e.target.files?.[0] ?? null)} /> {file && } ``` ### Fixed size inside a panel ```tsx ``` --- ## Caveats - **PDF export and large sheets:** PDF export captures only the virtualized visible rows. Export as `.xlsx` if you need all rows in a portable format. - **CSV multi-sheet:** CSV is single-sheet. Exporting a multi-sheet workbook to CSV exports only the active sheet. - **Column resize:** User column width changes are local state and are not reflected back through any prop. --- ## Live examples See the stories under **Data Display > Spreadsheet**.
